purpose: Keep RPLAN package, audit-certificate, compatibility, and consumer-rehearsal artifacts from becoming legal approval, adopted downstream contracts, or release readiness without the required owner evidence.

pitfalls.boundary: A passing audit certificate verifies only the declared profile, package hashes, context, source hashes, and lineage semantics; it is not legal approval, fairness proof, public-release approval, policy preference, or full redistricting acceptance.
RPLAN-local build, test, documentation, compatibility, or submodule success does not mean BISECT, RCOUNT, CROP, or future consumers have adopted a dependency contract.

Foundation changes that affect APIs, hashes, package formats, or audit semantics are not release-ready after RPLAN-local tests alone; affected changes require the RCOUNT rehearsal or an explicit scoped-out rationale.
